messages:
monitoring-bot: 🔔 ALERT: tool_call_errors spiked 8x in the last 2m; 95th p99 latency for /v1/invoke-tool at 3.2s. Error type: downstream timeouts (504). Affected models: redwood-open-7b and redwood-chat-8k. Highest traffic from tenants: tenant-42, tenant-free-ww.

sam: @here getting paged. seeing a lot of queued requests and KV eviction logs. tool workers overwhelmed, mem pressure on runtime nodes.

marta: copying metrics — backend retries up, and functioncall queue depth > 2k on worker-pool-3. can we soft-fail tool calls while we triage?

chris: +1 to short-circuit. recommend 3-tier mitigation: 1) immediate per-tenant rate cap for free tier, 2) disable structured_output for affected models, 3) skyline: emergency routed to cheap-sync fallback model.

sam: ok. doing step 1 now — patching quota for tenant-free-ww to 5rps and tenant-42 to 20rps. using admin API.

sam: runbook command I used:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/v1/tenants/tenant-free-ww/quota -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"max_rps":5}'
```

ops-bot: deploy started: quota-change-service v3.2.1 -> succeeded on region-us-east-1

marta: step 1 done for both tenants. observing - request rate dropped 70% from tenant-free-ww. tool error rate still elevated, likely queued state on workers.

chris: stepping in to toggle structured output for the two models. we'll turn off structured output + function_call preference so agents fall back to plain streaming text. This reduces RPC overhead.

sam: where's the flag?

chris: in featureflags service: `ff.env.model.tooling.structured_output` scoped by model-id. I'll flip for redwood-open-7b and redwood-chat-8k.

chris: command:
```
curl -X PATCH https://ff.internal/v1/flags/model -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" -d '{"model_ids": ["redwood-open-7b","redwood-chat-8k"], "structured_output": false}'
```

ops-bot: flag update applied; change rolled to 6/8 rollout nodes in us-east; scheduling remaining nodes.

marta: immediate improvement in avg tail latency for tool invocations where structured output used to be high. queue drain rate improving.

customer-success: FYI — I see ~12 customers with recent errors. I'll draft a short message for impacted tenants and hold until we confirm stabilization.

sam: good plan. we also need ephemeral routing to stop sending new tool calls to the overloaded worker-pool-3. I'm going to add a route rule to blacklist pool-3 for tool endpoints.

chris: safe to do. patching router rule now:
```
PATCH /routing/policies/active
body: {"rule": {"match": "worker_pool == 'pool-3' && endpoint == '/v1/invoke-tool'", "action": "deprioritize", "weight": 0}}
```
ops-bot: routing policy updated (deprioritize applied). new requests will avoid pool-3 within 30s.

marta: metrics: queue depth decreased 65% in 90s, tool_call_errors down 60% over 3m. KV cache evictions reduced.

sam: paging note: I'll escalate to the oncall handoff — @eli (oncall) you are up in 15m, handing this over with current mitigations in place. Please monitor the following: queue depth, tool_call_errors, structured_output_flag state, and customer error list.

eli (oncall): ack. I'll be on a short overlap. can you add an entry to the incident channel with customer list + suggested comms? also confirm rollback plan for flags and quotas.

marta: added incident stub in #incidents and pasted the 12-tenant list. rollback plan: 1) gradually revert routing rule -> reweight pool-3 by 10% steps, 2) re-enable structured_output per-model after 15min of stable error rate < 10% of baseline, 3) restore tenant quotas to previous values by policy.

chris: FYI — there is a subtlety: re-enabling structured_output can spike memory usage; recommended to re-enable one model at a time and watch GC/eviction graphs.

sam: customer-success drafted message, short and engineering-friendly:
"We're aware some requests may return errors or be slow. We've applied temporary rate-limits and disabled structured output for two models to restore service. We're monitoring and will update in 30m."

customer-success: sending to affected tenants now. will post copy to #customers-comms.

eli (oncall): I'll keep the mitigation active and monitor for 1h. if metrics stay below thresholds, we'll start stepwise rollback. assigning follow-ups:
- sam: confirm queues fully drained and note any persistent tenant offenders
- marta: track GC/evictions and memory on pool-3
- chris: prepare staged re-enable script for structured output
- customer-success: follow-up comms at 30m and 60m

sam: noted. adding shortterm tweak: increase eviction threshold on pool-3 by 5% to help queue drain (experimental).

ops-bot: config change applied to node-group pool-3: eviction_threshold -> 0.55

marta: small blip at +2m after eviction tweak but then smoothing. overall trend positive.

eli (oncall): thumbs up. I'll mark incident as "mitigated" in the tracker but keep pager on. If you see any regression ping me directly. Thanks team :heart:

monitoring-bot: UPDATE: tool_call_errors dropped to 0.9x baseline; p99 latency 0.9s for /v1/invoke-tool; queue depth normalized.

sam: resolving my pager. leaving notes in the incident doc with commands and rollback steps. good work everyone.

chris: follow-up action: schedule short postmortem to assess longer-term quotas, routing resilience, and whether structured_output should be gated per-tenant by default.

customer-success: customers acknowledged — one asked for ETA on full restore; told them we'll try staged re-enable in 30-60m once metrics stable.

eli (oncall): handoff complete. I'll update here if anything else happens. end of thread.
